title.narrative: Healthy and Empowered Youths Accessing better Resilient Livelihoods in Terego District (HEAL)

description.narrative: 1. Strengthen local education (including provision of comprehensive sexuality education), cultural and religious institutions, and community structures for increased access to correct and non-judgmental sexuality information. 2. Strengthen local health facilities and structures for stimulation of provision of essential youth friendly services including pregnancy prevention, safe pregnancy, safe deliveries, post abortion care, psychosocial counselling, child and mother health care, and basic material needs. 3. Empower communities to challenge negative social cultural norms that promote teenage pregnancy and child marriage. 4. Empower teen mother groups to establish and run environmentally friendly businesses. Using our successful integrated approach incorporating personal development, business development and facilitating the enabling environment, we will support teen mothers to become young social and green entrepreneurs. 5. Capacity Strengthening for the SRHR Alliance

According to the Ministry of Health in Uganda, 25% of Ugandan teenagers become pregnant by 19 years and often continue to give birth to many children until their mid-forties due to limited access to family planning. Consequently, maternal mortality and infant mortality remain high. The situation is even worse in refugee settlements and host communities in the West Nile sub region with Terego and Yumbe district recording the highest rates of teenage pregnancies and child marriages in Uganda (UNICEF, 2020). The early onset of first pregnancies is attributed to limited access to correct sexuality information that is youth friendly, life skills, modern contraceptives/ family planning, negative socio-cultural norms and practices among other things. In addition, low incomes and hunger are said to cause young girls to trade sex for survival, and some parents giving away their young girls for marriage in exchange for food and money. The increasing food insecurity is due to climate change that has increased volatility in the weather conditions affecting agriculture which is the major livelihood activity.
young people 10 to 24 years in and out of school, education and health service providers, key decision makers, parents and community leaders

title.narrative: Climate Resilience
The project integrates climate risks in programming

description.narrative: The integration of climate risks in programming includes an undertaking of concrete actions to reduce and/or mitigate risks related to climate change impact and disaster risks ( for example droughts, erosion, salinization, flooding, etc.) The projects we refer to could be on the themes of health education, justice, security, disaster management, finance and livelihoods.
